title: Lightweight function-call shim: ergonomic async iterators, partial-schema hints, and retry coordinator
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Build a small, language-idiomatic shim for function/tool calls that: 1) exposes ergonomic streaming result consumption (async iterators for JS/Python, channel/reader for Go), 2) performs fast partial schema hints during generation to fail-fast on obviously invalid shapes while allowing lean runtime coercion for minor inconsistencies, and 3) centralizes retry/backoff coordination for transient invocation errors and streaming mid-flight recoveries. This is intended as an SDK-level helper (not a full runtime rewrite) that developer-facing client libraries can call to simplify function invocation patterns across Python, TypeScript, and Go clients.
acceptance_criteria:
- SDKs expose a single helper API per language that: (a) accepts a function schema + call payload, (b) returns a streaming-first consumer with an ergonomic surface (async iterator in JS/Py, Reader/Channel in Go) and a convenience to materialize final value.
- Partial-schema validator: detects common errors (missing required props, type-mismatch in scalar fields) in <10ms for typical small schemas and surfaces a clear ValidationError. Allows opt-in strict mode to reject non-exact shapes.
- Retry coordinator: implements idempotency-aware retries with exponential backoff + full jitter, and supports streaming resume where the model/runtime can replay from last-acked token/KV position.
- Unit tests cover: success streams, mid-stream transient failures + resume, strict vs permissive schema modes, and cross-language parity tests.
- End-to-end example apps updated in repo showing Python/TS/Go usage.
- Metrics: emission of invocation.latency_ms, invocation.retries, invocation.partial_schema_errors.
- API documented in SDK reference and quickstart snippets in the README.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions and API shapes: 
- JS/TS: export function callWithSchema(schema, payload, opts?) -> { stream: AsyncIterable<Chunk>, collect(): Promise<Value>, cancel(): void }
  - stream yields partial chunks as they arrive (token/text/chunk), chunk objects include sequence id for resume.
  - opts.retry: { maxAttempts, baseMs, maxMs, idempotent: boolean } default to {3, 100, 10000, false}.
  - opts.validation: { mode: 'permissive'|'strict'|'hint-only' } where 'hint-only' runs a fast partial check that emits warnings but does not block.
- Python: async def call_with_schema(...): returns AsyncIterator[Chunk] and provides convenience awaitable collect() in helper class; sync wrapper uses threads and blocking iterator for sync users.
- Go: provide CallWithSchema(ctx, schema, payload, opts) -> (chan Chunk, CancelFunc) and a helper StreamReader that implements io.Reader for simple use cases.
- Partial schema validator: a lightweight wasm-friendly subset (TypeScript reference) and a compiled Go/Python port; it only validates scalar types and presence of required keys; nested object checks are shallow by default to keep latency low.
- Retry/resume: recharge token-level checkpointing uses per-chunk sequence ids that the runtime will accept in resume flows. If runtime doesn't support resume, fall back to full-retry with idempotency gating.
- Telemetry: emit stats via existing SDK telemetry client: invocation.attempts, invocation.resume_attempts, invocation.validation_warnings, invocation.validation_errors. Tag with model, region, schema_hash.
- Safety: default opts avoid automatic retries for non-idempotent calls; documentation required to instruct customers on marking idempotent functions.
- Compatibility: keep public surface minimal so it can be backported to older SDK releases; internal helpers can be extended later with richer validation/transform pipelines.
